title: How do I pay off a borrower's Auto Loans loan today from their PCB checking account?
content:
# How do I pay off a borrower's Auto Loans loan today from their PCB checking account?

This entry of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower asks to pay an auto loan off today by a transfer from their own PCB checking account. It is handled on the borrower's request.

## Policy

1. The agent posts one payment of payment type payoff, for the payoff amount, on today's credit date.
2. The payoff never collects a fee assessed contrary to the Auto Loans charter.
3. **Entry condition.** Every late charge on an installment left unpaid by an autopay debit presented to a closed source account has been waived before the payoff amount is fixed. Where that does not yet hold, the payoff amount is not fixed.

Observable effect for the borrower: the loan shows as paid off, with the lien release marked as pending.

## Tool: post_payoff_payment_63569e96

**Situation of use and capability.** Posts a payoff payment that the borrower pays today by transfer from their own PCB checking account, closing the auto loan. One call books the payment on the loan's activity as a payoff made by PCB transfer, split into the fees, interest and principal parts given, and books the matching fee settlement entry when the fees part is above zero. On the loan it sets the unpaid principal and fees to 0.00, records today as the last payment date and as the closing date, marks the loan paid off with no installment due and no days past due, and marks the lien release as pending.

**How it is invoked.** An internal tool of the agent: it must first be unlocked with unlock_agent_discoverable_tool and then called with call_agent_discoverable_tool.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| auto_loan_id | the auto loan reference number of the loan being paid off, from the auto loan lookup | reference number |
| amount | the total payoff payment drawn from the checking account | USD, 2 decimal places |
| fees_portion | the part of the payment applied to fees due | USD, 2 decimal places; 0.00 when no fees are due |
| interest_portion | the part of the payment applied to accrued interest | USD, 2 decimal places |
| principal_portion | the part of the payment applied to principal | USD, 2 decimal places |
| counterparty_account_id | the checking account reference number of the borrower's PCB checking account the money is drawn from, from the checking account lookup | reference number |

**Return.** On success the receipt shows status "paid_off" with: payment_reference (the 12-digit payment reference number), auto_txn_id (reference number of the payoff entry), fee_settlement_id (reference number of the fee settlement entry, or empty when the fees part is 0.00), closed_date (today, YYYY-MM-DD) and lien_status ("release_pending").

## Basis Q&A

**Can the payoff include a fee that should never have been charged?** No. The payoff never collects a fee assessed contrary to the charter.

**What shows that the call worked?** A receipt with status "paid_off", the payment reference number, and the lien release shown as pending.
